topic: UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India

questions.stem: INDIA currently has how many UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITES (as of 2024)?

options.option_text: 43 — 35 Cultural + 7 Natural + 1 Mixed; India = 6TH LARGEST list globally after Italy, China, Germany, France, Spain

questions.explanation: UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITES in INDIA — as of 2024: 43 SITES (35 CULTURAL + 7 NATURAL + 1 MIXED). INDIA = 6TH LARGEST World Heritage list globally (after Italy 59, China 57, Germany 52, France 53, Spain 50). UNESCO World Heritage programme est. 1972 Convention (Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural + Natural Heritage, Paris); operates under UNESCO (UN Education, Science, Culture Organization). FIRST INDIAN sites (1983, 4 together): AJANTA CAVES (Maharashtra), ELLORA CAVES (Maharashtra), AGRA FORT (UP), TAJ MAHAL (UP). INDIA's 43 SITES (selective): (1) TAJ MAHAL (1983) — Shah Jahan's mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal, 1632-53, Agra. (2) AGRA FORT (1983). (3) AJANTA CAVES (1983) — 29 Buddhist cave-temples 2nd c. BCE-6th c. CE; paintings. (4) ELLORA CAVES (1983) — 34 Hindu-Buddhist-Jain caves, inc. Kailasa Temple. (5) KONARK SUN TEMPLE (1984) — Odisha, 13th c. Narasimhadeva I. (6) GROUP OF MONUMENTS, MAHABALIPURAM (1984) — Pallava, Tamil Nadu. (7) KAZIRANGA NATIONAL PARK (1985, Natural) — Assam, one-horned rhino. (8) KEOLADEO NP (1985, N) — Bharatpur, birds. (9) MANAS WILDLIFE SANCTUARY (1985, N) — Assam. (10) CHURCHES + CONVENTS OF GOA (1986) — Old Goa, Portuguese Baroque. (11) KHAJURAHO (1986) — Chandela sculpted temples MP. (12) HAMPI (1986) — Vijayanagar ruins, Karnataka. (13) FATEHPUR SIKRI (1986) — Akbar's short-lived capital. (14) ELEPHANTA CAVES (1987) — Mumbai, Shiva rock-cut. (15) GREAT LIVING CHOLA TEMPLES (1987) — Brihadeshvara Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram, Airavatesvara Darasuram. (16) PATTADAKAL (1987) — Chalukya temples. (17) SUNDARBANS NP (1987, N) — tigers, mangroves. (18) NANDA DEVI + VALLEY OF FLOWERS NP (1988 extended 2005, N) — Uttarakhand. (19) BUDDHIST MONUMENTS SANCHI (1989) — Ashoka stupa, MP. (20) QUTB MINAR COMPLEX (1993) — Delhi. (21) HUMAYUN's TOMB (1993) — Delhi. (22) MOUNTAIN RAILWAYS OF INDIA (1999, 2005, 2008) — Darjeeling HR, Nilgiri Mountain Railway, Kalka-Shimla Railway. (23) MAHABODHI TEMPLE COMPLEX BODH GAYA (2002) — Bihar. (24) ROCK SHELTERS OF BHIMBETKA (2003) — MP, pre-historic art 30000 yrs old. (25) CHAMPANER-PAVAGADH (2004) — Gujarat. (26) CHATRAPATI SHIVAJI TERMINUS (2004) — Mumbai. (27) RED FORT COMPLEX (2007) — Delhi. (28) JANTAR MANTAR (2010) — Jaipur. (29) WESTERN GHATS (2012, N) — 39 properties across 6 states. (30) HILL FORTS OF RAJASTHAN (2013) — Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Jaisalmer, Gagron, Amer. (31) RANI-KI-VAV (2014) — Patan Gujarat. (32) GREAT HIMALAYAN NP (2014, N) — HP. (33) ARCHAEOLOGICAL SITE OF NALANDA (2016) — Bihar. (34) KHANGCHENDZONGA NP (2016, Mixed) — Sikkim. (35) CAPITOL COMPLEX CHANDIGARH (2016) — Le Corbusier. (36) HISTORIC CITY OF AHMEDABAD (2017) — first Indian city. (37) VICTORIAN GOTHIC + ART DECO ENSEMBLES MUMBAI (2018). (38) PINK CITY JAIPUR (2019). (39) KAKATIYA RUDRESHWARA (RAMAPPA) TEMPLE (2021) — Telangana. (40) DHOLAVIRA (2021) — Indus Valley, Gujarat. (41) SANTINIKETAN (2023) — Tagore's abode. (42) SACRED ENSEMBLES OF HOYSALA (2023) — Belur, Halebidu, Somnathapura. (43) MOIDAMS (2024) — Ahom royal burial mounds, Assam (44th site inscribed at Delhi WHC 2024).

questions.stem: The TAJ MAHAL, UNESCO-listed in 1983, was built by:

options.option_text: SHAH JAHAN (1632-1653) — mausoleum for wife MUMTAZ MAHAL; main architect USTAD AHMAD LAHAURI; 20,000 workers; one of 7 Wonders of World (2007)

questions.explanation: TAJ MAHAL — 'Crown of Palaces' — most iconic monument of India. LOCATION: AGRA, Uttar Pradesh, on south bank of Yamuna River. BUILT by SHAH JAHAN (Mughal Emperor 1628-58) as MAUSOLEUM for his beloved WIFE MUMTAZ MAHAL (Arjumand Banu Begum, died 17 June 1631 giving birth to 14th child GAUHARA Begum at Burhanpur). CONSTRUCTION: started 1632 (foundations + main mausoleum 1632-1643); whole complex completed ~1653 (21 YEARS). COST ~₹32 million then (~₹70 BILLION today). WORKFORCE: 20,000 labourers + craftsmen from India, Persia, Ottoman empire. MAIN ARCHITECT: USTAD AHMAD LAHAURI (from Lahore); with assistants from Persia + Turkey. MATERIALS: (a) WHITE MAKRANA MARBLE from Rajasthan (main); (b) RED SANDSTONE for adjacent buildings; (c) 28 TYPES of SEMI-PRECIOUS + PRECIOUS STONES — LAPIS LAZULI (Afghanistan), JADE (China), TURQUOISE (Tibet), SAPPHIRE (Sri Lanka), crystal (China), malachite, onyx, carnelian, amethyst, etc. INLAY technique = 'PIETRA DURA' (parchin kari). STRUCTURE: (1) GATEWAY (Darwaza-i-rauza) — red sandstone, massive. (2) CHAR BAGH (garden) — Persian 4-part quartered garden; reflecting pool with Taj mirrored; cypress trees (death) + fruit trees (life). (3) MAIN MAUSOLEUM on plinth — 4-sided symmetric; CENTRAL DOME (ONION-shaped, double-shelled, 35m high); 4 MINARETS (40m each, tilted slightly outwards so they fall away if earthquake hits). (4) Inside: cenotaphs of Mumtaz (centre) + Shah Jahan (off-centre, added later by Aurangzeb) under the dome; ACTUAL GRAVES in crypt below (closed to public). Walls inlaid with CALLIGRAPHY from Quran (by Abd al-Haqq Amanat Khan Shirazi). (5) MOSQUE (west) + GUEST HOUSE / Mehman Khana (east, symmetric counterpart). LEGENDS: (1) Black Taj myth — Shah Jahan planned a mirror-image in BLACK marble across river, never built (no historical evidence — likely romantic myth). (2) Architects' hands amputated — false myth. THREATS: (a) YELLOWING / pollution (SPM from Mathura refinery + Agra cottage industries; SC intervention — Taj Trapezium Zone Pollution case 1996); (b) wood foundation concerns; (c) tourist footfall wear (now regulated — entry capped 40,000/day with timed slots since 2018). RESTORATION ongoing — MUD PACK TREATMENT to clean marble; ASI + MOEF oversight. UNESCO WHS 1983; 'NEW 7 Wonders of the World' poll 2007 ranked it. 'A TEARDROP ON THE CHEEK OF TIME' — Rabindranath Tagore. 'THE PALACE OF LOVE' — romantic canon.

questions.stem: The WESTERN GHATS, added to UNESCO list in 2012, is a NATURAL heritage site stretching through:

options.option_text: 6 states — Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu (+ tiny Gujarat); 39 component properties listed by UNESCO

questions.explanation: WESTERN GHATS (SAHYADRI) — UNESCO NATURAL WORLD HERITAGE SITE inscribed 2012 — world's 8th biodiversity hotspot + one of the most biodiverse mountain ranges in the world. DIMENSIONS: ~1600 km long, parallel to west coast of India from Tapti River (Gujarat-Maharashtra border) to Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu). WIDTH 30-50 km; AVG ELEVATION 900-1500m; highest peak = ANAMUDI (Kerala) 2,695m. PASSES through 6 INDIAN STATES: (1) MAHARASHTRA — Bhimashankar, Mahabaleshwar, Western Ghats-Maharashtra. (2) GOA — Bhagwan Mahavir NP, Mhadei. (3) KARNATAKA — Agumbe (Cherrapunji of South), Kudremukh NP, Someshwara, Dandeli-Anshi (Kali Tiger Reserve), Mookambika WLS. (4) KERALA — Silent Valley NP, Anamudi, Eravikulam NP, Periyar NP (+ Tiger Reserve), Parambikulam TR. (5) TAMIL NADU — Nilgiris BR, Kalakkad-Mundanthurai TR, Indira Gandhi WLS, Mukurthi NP, Mundanthurai. (6) TINY in GUJARAT (north tip). UNESCO listed 39 COMPONENT PROPERTIES (7 sub-clusters). FEATURES: (a) 5,000+ FLOWERING plant species (35% ENDEMIC — found ONLY here); 100+ endemic species of orchids. (b) Home to NILGIRI TAHR (TN, Kerala — endemic), LION-TAILED MACAQUE (Kerala, Karnataka — endangered), NILGIRI LANGUR, MALABAR CIVET, PURPLE FROG (endemic, 'Mahony's frog'), KING COBRA, MALABAR PIED HORNBILL. (c) 508 bird species, 180 amphibians, 225 reptiles (60% endemic reptiles, 78% endemic amphibians). (d) Origin of peninsular rivers — GODAVARI, KRISHNA, KAVERI, TUNGABHADRA, PERIYAR, PAMBA, BHARATAPUZHA. (e) Dominant vegetation: tropical evergreen forests (SOUTH — Kerala, TN), semi-evergreen, tropical moist + dry deciduous, montane shola-grassland (unique stunted forests in valleys + grassland on hilltops). CHERRAPUNJI-equivalent wetness: AGUMBE Karnataka ~7500mm; MAHABALESHWAR Maharashtra ~6000mm. PROTECTED AREAS within: 20 NATIONAL PARKS, 68 WLS, several TIGER RESERVES (Periyar, Parambikulam, Kalakkad, Sathyamangalam, Bhadra, Bandipur, Dandeli-Anshi, Mudumalai, Wayanad). THREATS: deforestation, mining, hydropower projects, tourism, plantations, invasive species (Lantana, Eupatorium, Acacia). CONSERVATION: NIYAMGIRI case (2013, rejected mining), Madhav Gadgil Committee 2011 + KASTURIRANGAN Committee 2013 (recommended Ecologically Sensitive Area designation for 37% of Western Ghats — politically contested by states). 2021 Kerala + Karnataka floods blamed partly on deforestation + quarrying. Western Ghats = 'WATER TOWER of PENINSULAR INDIA'.

questions.stem: The KHAJURAHO GROUP OF MONUMENTS, UNESCO-listed in 1986, is famous for:

options.option_text: NAGARA-style HINDU + JAIN TEMPLES (10th-11th c.) with INTRICATE SCULPTURES including tantric + erotic motifs; built by CHANDELA dynasty

questions.explanation: KHAJURAHO GROUP OF MONUMENTS — UNESCO WHS 1986; complex of medieval Hindu + Jain TEMPLES at KHAJURAHO village, Chhatarpur district, MADHYA PRADESH. Built 950-1050 CE by CHANDELA dynasty rulers (esp. YASHOVARMAN + DHANGADEVA + VIDYADHARA). ORIGINALLY 85 temples built; 25 survive today. STYLE: NAGARA (North Indian) — characterised by shikhara (tower) rising to a single point; curvilinear outline; square sanctum; 5 sub-elements (mandovara, shikhara, garbhagriha, antarala, mandapa). Temples grouped: (1) WESTERN GROUP (largest + most famous) — 14 temples; includes KANDARIYA MAHADEVA (tallest, 31m, ~870 sculptures), LAXMANA, VISHVANATHA, CHITRAGUPTA. (2) EASTERN GROUP (Jain) — PARSHVANATHA, ADINATHA, GHANTAI. (3) SOUTHERN GROUP (smaller) — Duladeo, Chaturbhuj. FAMOUS SCULPTURES (5% of total is erotic): renowned for 'MITHUNA' (amorous couples) + tantric iconography — rightly framed in context of EPIC-MAHAKAVYA tradition, Kamasutra-era social philosophy + goddess-tantrism. Most sculptures show DAILY LIFE, gods, celestial beings, guardians, yogis, secular subjects; erotic only on OUTER walls of specific temples. ICONOGRAPHY also celebrates FEMININE DIVINITY + PROLIFIC life + worldly concerns leading up to moksha — conceptual framework of Kama, Artha, Dharma, Moksha of Hindu life-purposes. HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE: (1) Peak of NAGARA architecture before Islamic invasions (Ghurid, Ghaznavid, Delhi Sultanate from ~1200 onwards). (2) Chandelas were major N Indian power — competed with Cholas + Palas + Rashtrakutas. FORGOTTEN for 500 years under jungle; REDISCOVERED BY CAPTAIN T.S. BURT (British army) in 1838. Alexander Cunningham mapped in 1852. ASI conservation since 1920s. KHAJURAHO DANCE FESTIVAL — annual week-long classical dance festival (since 1975), held in Feb-Mar outdoors against temple backdrop; features Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Kathakali. Major cultural event; organized by MP Kala Parishad. RELATED Nagara-style heritage sites: KONARK SUN TEMPLE (Odisha 1984), SUN TEMPLE MODHERA (Gujarat, not WHS yet), LINGARAJA + Jagannath Puri (Odisha), Osian (Rajasthan), Bhubaneshwar Kalinga group, Kashi Vishwanath (rebuilt). DRAVIDA (South) style sites: Brihadeshvara, Mahabalipuram, Hampi, Pattadakal. VESARA (hybrid, Deccan) — Hoysala temples 2023 WHS.

questions.stem: The RANI-KI-VAV (Queen's Stepwell), UNESCO-listed in 2014 and FEATURED on the ₹100 currency note, is located at:

options.option_text: PATAN, Gujarat — built 1063 CE by Queen UDAYAMATI as memorial to Chalukya king BHIMDEV I; 7 levels of intricate sculptures + 500+ motifs

questions.explanation: RANI-KI-VAV (Queen's Stepwell) — at PATAN, Gujarat (formerly Anahilavada, medieval capital of Chalukyas/Solankis of Gujarat). BUILT ~1063 CE by QUEEN UDAYAMATI (widow of King BHIMDEV I of Chaulukya dynasty, ruled 1022-64) as MEMORIAL to her husband. STEPWELL (BAOLI / BAORI / VAV) = multi-level well structure with steps descending to water table, for water storage, community gathering, pilgrimage. Rani-ki-Vav is the GRANDEST stepwell in India. STRUCTURE: (1) 7 LEVELS of steps descending to well; (2) 64m long × 20m wide × 28m DEEP; (3) oriented EAST-WEST; (4) 500+ SCULPTURES + 1000+ smaller motifs; (5) themes from HINDU MYTHOLOGY — DASHAVATARA of Vishnu (10 incarnations — Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana, Parashurama, Rama, Krishna, Buddha, Kalki), plus scenes from Ramayana + Mahabharata; (6) APSARAS (celestial nymphs), yoginis, Brahmanic + tantric figures; (7) Seshashayi Vishnu (reclining Vishnu) at bottom. FATE: flooded + silted by SARASWATI river changes; rediscovered + excavated by ASI (1940s-1980s). Restored extensively. INSCRIBED on UNESCO World Heritage in 2014. Featured on INDIA's ₹100 CURRENCY NOTE (introduced in new Mahatma Gandhi series 2018). SIGNIFICANCE: (1) unique MARU-GURJARA / SOLANKI architectural style; (2) INVERTED TEMPLE form — unique in world architecture; (3) cultural + engineering achievement. OTHER FAMOUS STEPWELLS in INDIA: (1) CHAND BAORI (Abhaneri, Rajasthan) — ~800-900 CE, 3500 narrow steps, 13 storeys, 100ft deep — deepest stepwell. (2) AGRASEN KI BAOLI (Delhi, 14th c.) — 60m × 15m, atmospheric. (3) DADA HARIR STEPWELL (Ahmedabad, 1499, Queen Harir). (4) ADALAJ STEPWELL (Gujarat, 1499, Rudabai) — 5 storeys, Islamic + Hindu motifs. (5) RAJON KI BAOLI (Delhi, Lodi-era, 16th c.). (6) ROYAL STEPWELL (Dholavira IVC). (7) Raniji ki Baori + 100+ baoris in Bundi, Rajasthan. TRADITIONAL PURPOSE: (a) water for drinking + bathing + rituals; (b) cool sanctuary in hot summer; (c) gathering place for women (who fetched water); (d) TEMPLE SHRINE at water's edge (Vav = 'stepwell' OR 'wading place' OR 'well of wisdom'); (e) fort / caravanserai on trade routes. DECLINED with modern piped water + pumps; 1000s of stepwells abandoned → filled with debris. REVIVAL movements trying to restore them.

questions.stem: SANTINIKETAN, inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List in 2023, is associated with:

options.option_text: RABINDRANATH TAGORE — founded Visva-Bharati University here in 1921; Asia's first Nobel Laureate for Literature (Gitanjali, 1913)

questions.explanation: SANTINIKETAN ('Abode of Peace') — UNESCO WHS 2023; the place immortalised by RABINDRANATH TAGORE (1861-1941) — poet, playwright, novelist, painter, composer, educator, Nobel Laureate. LOCATION: Birbhum district, West Bengal (~160 km from Kolkata). HISTORY: (1) 1862 — Tagore's father DEBENDRANATH TAGORE established 'Santiniketan Ashram' as meditation retreat on 20 acres donated by Raipur zamindars. (2) 1901 — Tagore (age 40) established experimental school 'Patha Bhavana' with 5 students (including his son Rathindranath) — open-air, nature-based education; students sat UNDER TREES. (3) 1913 — Tagore awarded NOBEL PRIZE in LITERATURE for GITANJALI ('Song Offerings', trans by Tagore + W.B. Yeats); FIRST ASIAN NOBEL LAUREATE in any field; only INDIAN Nobel in Lit until now. (4) 1921 — founded VISVA-BHARATI UNIVERSITY ('world university'); motto 'YATRA VISHVAM BHAVATYEKA NIDAM' ('where the world makes a home in a single nest'). (5) 1951 — declared CENTRAL UNIVERSITY by Indian Parliament; PM = Visitor, Prez = Visitor. TAGORE's VISION: (a) BREAK walls between disciplines — arts + music + literature + science + agriculture + rural reconstruction; (b) BENGALI + Indian cultural resurgence; (c) UNIVERSAL humanism; (d) INDO-foreign dialogue — foreign scholars invited (Leonard Elmhirst, Arthur Geddes, Christopher Isherwood, Aldous Huxley, Yukteswar Giri, Einstein's interactions). ICONIC STRUCTURES + FACULTIES: (a) KALA BHAVANA (Institute of Fine Arts) — nurtured NANDALAL BOSE, BINODE BIHARI MUKHERJEE, RAMKINKAR BAIJ (sculptor of 'Santhal Family' + 'Mill Call'), Satyajit Ray, K.G. Subramanyan. (b) SANGIT BHAVANA (music) — home of RABINDRA SANGEET. (c) PATHA BHAVANA (open-air school); (d) UTTARAYANA (Tagore's residence complex: Udayana, Shyamali, Punascha, Udichi, Konark houses; museum); (e) CHHATIMTALA (meditation tree grove). (f) VISHWA-BHARATI Library. TAGORE AUTHORED national anthems of INDIA ('JANA GANA MANA', first sung 1911 at Cong Calcutta session, adopted 1950) + BANGLADESH ('Amar Sonar Bangla', 1971) + strongly influenced Sri Lanka's anthem ('Sri Lanka Matha', by his student Ananda Samarakoon, 1940). RENOUNCED KNIGHTHOOD (1919 after Jallianwala Bagh). Called 'GURUDEV' by Gandhi, 'Bishwokobi' (World Poet). His paintings developed after age 65. FESTIVALS at Santiniketan: POUSH MELA (Dec, 3 days), BASANTA UTSAV (Holi), VARSHAMANGAL (monsoon). STUDENTS: Indira Gandhi, Amartya Sen, Satyajit Ray (trained in Kala Bhavana), Ritwik Ghatak, Suchitra Mitra. SANTINIKETAN was a STRONG CONTENDER for WHS list since 2010; finally inscribed at Riyadh (Saudi Arabia) WHC meeting, 17 Sep 2023.

questions.stem: HAMPI (UNESCO 1986), a UNESCO World Heritage site with spectacular ruins, was the capital of which empire?

options.option_text: VIJAYANAGAR EMPIRE (1336-1646) — razed after BATTLE OF TALIKOTA 1565 by combined Deccan Sultanates

questions.explanation: HAMPI — UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986; initially 'endangered' list, removed 2006 after improvement). Ruins of the VIJAYANAGAR EMPIRE's capital (1336-1565), on south bank of Tungabhadra River, Ballari district, Karnataka. Area: 41.5 sq km; ~1,600 monuments. HISTORY: (1) 1336 — founded by HARIHARA + BUKKA brothers with blessing of sage Vidyaranya on ruins of earlier Anegondi settlement. (2) Peak 1500s under KRISHNADEVARAYA (1509-29) — Portuguese traveller DOMINGO PAES (1520) called it 'as large as Rome + much more beautiful to the sight'. (3) DESTROYED by combined armies of 4 DECCAN SULTANATES (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar) at BATTLE OF TALIKOTA (23 Jan 1565); last ruler RAMA RAYA killed; city razed over 6 months. Never recovered. KEY MONUMENTS: (1) VIRUPAKSHA TEMPLE — ONLY temple still in active worship (pre-dates Vijayanagar, 7th c. Pallava origin; expanded by Vijayanagar); 50m main gopura. (2) VITTALA TEMPLE complex — 16th c., famous STONE CHARIOT (facing it) + MUSICAL PILLARS (musical sounds when tapped; 'saptaswara' pillars). Iconic image. (3) LOTUS MAHAL (royal pavilion, Indo-Islamic fusion). (4) ELEPHANT STABLES (11 domed chambers). (5) HAZARA RAMA TEMPLE (private chapel of royal family, 1000s of Rama reliefs). (6) KRISHNA TEMPLE complex. (7) QUEEN's BATH. (8) ACHYUTARAYA Temple. (9) NARASIMHA monolith (6.7m). (10) BADAVI LINGA. (11) Royal Enclosure + Mahanavami Dibba platform. (12) Talarigatta Gateway. (13) SASIVEKALU + KADALEKALU GANESHA monoliths. (14) Tungabhadra bridge ruins. BAZAARS: Virupaksha Bazaar (to main temple), Sule Bazaar, Krishna Bazaar — each once bustling with international traders (Portuguese, Arab, Persian, Chinese). LIVING HERITAGE at Hampi — PUSHPA RATHAYATRA festival continues; small village ANEGUNDI across river preserves traditions. LANDSCAPE: huge BOULDER-STREWN terrain — distinctive; dry arid Deccan with Tungabhadra providing water. ASI + Karnataka govt + UNESCO support conservation. TOURISM hit by 2019 Tungabhadra flooding; infrastructure expanding. Nearby sites: (1) HOSPETE town; (2) TUNGABHADRA DAM (1953); (3) ANEGUNDI. Hampi is one of India's most PHOTOGENIC sites — ruins against orange-red boulders + green paddy + blue river. Bollywood + international filming (PS-1, Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam, Guru).

questions.stem: AJANTA CAVES (UNESCO 1983), famous for Buddhist rock-cut paintings + sculptures, are in:

options.option_text: MAHARASHTRA — Aurangabad district; 30 caves; 2nd c. BCE-6th c. CE; Jataka-tale murals; rediscovered 1819 by British soldier John Smith

questions.explanation: AJANTA CAVES — 30 BUDDHIST rock-cut cave temples + monasteries carved into a horseshoe-shaped cliff along the WAGHORA river valley, at AJANTA village, Aurangabad district, MAHARASHTRA. DATED: two phases — (1) 2nd c. BCE to 1st c. CE (Hinayana phase, caves 9, 10, 12, 13, 15A). (2) 5th c.-6th c. CE (Mahayana phase, most others — Gupta era; Vakataka patronage). ABANDONED + forgotten by 7th c.; lost to jungle. REDISCOVERED 28 April 1819 by a British Army officer CAPTAIN JOHN SMITH of the 28th Cavalry while hunting TIGER; carved his name + date in Cave 10 (graffiti still visible!). Subsequently surveyed by James Fergusson, Major Gill, Robert Gill (who documented 30 caves for 27 years, most lost in 1866 fire), John Griffiths (1872 onwards — copies again lost in 1885 fire at Imperial Institute London). Most of original copies now at Victoria + Albert Museum London. UNESCO WHS 1983. SIGNIFICANCE: (1) BEST-preserved examples of ANCIENT INDIAN PAINTING + SCULPTURE in the world. (2) Masterpieces of Buddhist religious art. KEY CAVES: (1) CAVE 1 — Mahayana era (5th c.); 'PADMAPANI' (Bodhisattva with lotus) mural — most famous painting in India; exquisite facial expression, serene meditation, 'compassion personified'. Also 'VAJRAPANI' (Bodhisattva with thunderbolt). (2) CAVE 2 — Jataka scenes. (3) CAVE 10 — Hinayana chaitya (stupa hall); earliest paintings (2nd c. BCE-ish). (4) CAVE 16 — 'MAHAJANAKA JATAKA' (Prince abandoning worldly life). (5) CAVE 17 — 'VESSANTARA JATAKA' + 'SHIBI JATAKA' (compassionate king gives flesh to eagle). (6) CAVE 19 — chaitya with superb facade. (7) CAVE 26 — reclining Buddha + parinirvana scene. TECHNIQUE: frescoes (Tempera on lime-plaster + clay-hair mixture base); vegetable + mineral pigments (lapis lazuli, ochre). Colours preserved 1500+ years due to cave microclimate. THEMES: mostly JATAKA tales (previous lives of Buddha), life of Buddha, Buddhist deities, court life, everyday scenes, nature, animals, apsaras. STYLE: vibrant, tactile, emotive — 'the birth of Indian classical painting'; influenced entire East Asian Buddhist art (Dunhuang, Bamiyan, Afghanistan + Central Asia caves). RELATED: ELLORA CAVES (100 km away, UNESCO 1983) — 34 caves (Buddhist + Hindu + Jain, 6-10th c.) — even more varied. PITALKHORA + BHAJA + KARLE + KANHERI + NASIK — other Buddhist rock-cut sites in Maharashtra. INDIAN rock-cut tradition = world's finest; ~1,200 rock-cut caves in India.

questions.stem: The KONARK SUN TEMPLE (UNESCO 1984) is shaped like a giant CHARIOT of the Sun God, with:

options.option_text: 24 CARVED WHEELS + 7 HORSES pulling the chariot — representing 24 hrs/day + 7 days of week; built 13th c. by NARASIMHADEVA I of Eastern Ganga

questions.explanation: KONARK SUN TEMPLE (Surya Devalaya) — one of India's greatest temples; UNESCO WHS 1984. LOCATION: Konark, Puri district, ODISHA, on the Bay of Bengal coast. BUILT: 1238-1264 CE by KING NARASIMHADEVA I (r. 1238-1264) of EASTERN GANGA dynasty — to COMMEMORATE his military victories. DESIGNED as colossal STONE CHARIOT of SURYA (Sun God): (a) 24 EXQUISITELY CARVED WHEELS (2 sets of 12 on each side) — symbolism debated: 24 hrs of day, 12 months × 2 (solstices), or 12 zodiac signs × 2 halves; wheels function as SUNDIALS too (shadow cast on spokes tells time). (b) 7 HORSES pulling the chariot — representing 7 days of the week + 7 colours of the rainbow + Sun's 7 rays. (c) Temple stands on raised platform. NAME 'KONARK' = 'KONA' (corner) + 'ARKA' (sun). Dedicated to Surya, whose chariot is pulled by 7 horses in Hindu mythology. STRUCTURE: (1) DEUL / SHIKHARA (main tower) — originally 70m tall; COLLAPSED (partially early 1600s, entirely by 1837); only dattoraam + anunated walls remain (still 30m). (2) JAGMOHAN (porch/mandapa) — INTACT 38m tall, pyramidal. (3) NATA MANDIR (dance hall) — ruins. (4) Bhoga Mandira (offering hall) — partial. MATERIAL: khondalite stone (ferruginous, weathered, red-brown). CARVINGS: outer walls carved with intricate sculptures — erotic motifs, dancers, musicians, daily life, aquatic scenes, animals, gods, celestial beings — rivalling Khajuraho. PROBLEMS: (1) PARTIAL collapse of main tower (possibly built on weak base; some say struck by lightning; some say Muslim invaders; some say sinking base; debated). (2) SEA encroachment (sand-filling of interior by 1903 British to arrest further collapse). (3) Today remains standing + major tourist draw. KONARK was called 'BLACK PAGODA' (kalakhet pagoda) by European sailors — darker than Puri's 'White Pagoda' (Jagannath temple). SURYA idol originally stood in sanctum — unclear fate (destroyed or moved; current statue in Delhi National Museum). KONARK DANCE FESTIVAL — annual 5-day classical dance festival (December) held in temple grounds — Odissi, Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Chhau, Manipuri. TAGORE wrote: 'Here the language of stone surpasses the language of man'. ODISHA'S 3-TEMPLE 'GOLDEN TRIANGLE': Konark + Puri Jagannath + Bhubaneswar (Lingaraja). Nearby Chandrabhaga beach, Ramachandi temple.

questions.stem: DHOLAVIRA, UNESCO-inscribed in 2021, is a major archaeological site of the:

options.option_text: INDUS VALLEY / HARAPPAN CIVILISATION (2600-1900 BCE) — Khadir Bet, Gujarat; sophisticated water management + urban planning

questions.explanation: DHOLAVIRA — UNESCO WHS 2021 (added in Fuzhou, China online session). INDUS VALLEY CIVILISATION (IVC / Harappan) site on KHADIR BET island in the RANN OF KUTCH, Gujarat. 4th or 5th LARGEST IVC site (after Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Rakhigarhi + possibly Ganeriwala). DATED: ~3000-1500 BCE; 7 cultural stages identified. DISCOVERED 1967-68 by J.P. JOSHI of ASI. Fully excavated 1989 onwards by R.S. BISHT (ASI Director of Excavations). SIGNIFICANCE: (1) UNIQUE urban planning — 3 divisions (Citadel + Middle town + Lower town); (2) SOPHISTICATED WATER MANAGEMENT — 16 HUGE reservoirs (largest 73m × 29m × 10m deep!) capturing monsoon run-off + spring + groundwater; DAM, storm-water drains, check dams; RAINWATER HARVESTING on heroic scale (critical in arid zone receiving only 300mm rain). Largest reservoir system in IVC. (3) MAJOR SIGNBOARD — 10-character Indus script sign (each ~37 cm tall!) — world's earliest SIGNBOARD of its size; hung like a modern signboard, believed to be above gateway; letters carved on wooden boards inlaid with gypsum. INDUS SCRIPT remains undeciphered. (4) Extensive TRADE — seals, beads (agate, carnelian), copper objects — linked to Mesopotamia, Elam, Magan (Oman). (5) DEFENSIVE WALLS of massive stones (up to 18m thick at base); not seen at most other IVC sites. (6) ADVANCED 'STADIUM' or ceremonial ground (283m × 47m) — may have been ritual space. MATERIALS: built of CUT + DRESSED STONES (unusual — most IVC sites use mud-brick), plaster, some baked brick. OTHER MAJOR HARAPPAN SITES in India: (1) LOTHAL (Gujarat — first tidal DOCKYARD, Maritime Museum coming up, UNESCO tentative list); (2) RAKHIGARHI (Haryana — likely LARGEST IVC site, 550 hectares; 2019 DNA study on skeletons); (3) KALIBANGAN (Rajasthan — world's earliest ploughed field, fire altars); (4) BANAWALI (Haryana); (5) SURKOTADA (Gujarat — earliest evidence of horse?); (6) ROPAR (Punjab); (7) ALAMGIRPUR (UP — eastern-most); (8) MEHRGARH (Balochistan, Pakistan — precursor, 7000 BCE). FAMOUS FOREIGN SITES: MOHENJO-DARO + HARAPPA (both in Pakistan), GANWERIWALA (Pakistan). Total ~2000 IVC SITES identified; most in India post-partition. IVC covered ~1.5 million sq km — larger than contemporary Mesopotamia + Egypt COMBINED. Characteristics: planned cities, script, grid roads, drainage, standardised weights + measures, fire altars, no temples/palaces identified, terracotta figurines (Mother Goddess, Pashupati seal, Dancing Girl bronze, bearded priest-king steatite), bath complex at Mohenjo-daro, granaries.
